1.say: Grip the blue-and-red wire stripper and strip about one centimeter off the end of each white wire. Lay the two stripped white wires apart on the mat with copper tips exposed.
placements: left white insulated C-shaped wire → stripped about 1 cm / 3/8 inch at its lower tip with blue-and-red stripper jaws closed around insulation, copper exposed at bottom-center; in the video: left side of blue-gray mat

right white insulated C-shaped wire → stripped about 1 cm at its lower tip with blue-and-red stripper jaws closed around insulation, copper exposed facing left wire; in the video: right side of blue-gray mat
watch_for: if bare copper is much longer than 1 cm you stripped too much, cut and re-strip shorter
if copper strands look nicked or cut short the stripper cut the metal, re-strip on a fresh section
1.check_yourself: Two separate white wires lie apart on the mat with about one centimeter of copper exposed at each joining end.
1.safety: Keep fingers clear of the stripper jaws and pull away from your skin.

2.say: Push the two copper ends together end-to-end in the middle of the mat. Twist the bare copper around the join until it locks into a neat twist.
placements: left white wire copper end → pushed end-to-end against right white wire copper end at bottom-center to form one loop; in the video: bottom-center of blue mat
right white wire copper end → twisted 2-3 turns around left copper end to lock, using fingers on white insulation; in the video: small copper twist at bottom-center
watch_for: if the wires pull apart with a light tug the twist is too loose, push together and twist tighter
if white insulation is twisted instead of copper you gripped too far back, twist only the bare copper
2.check_yourself: The two white wires form one loop with the copper ends twisted into a small tight join.

3.say: Hold the white wire loop steady by the white insulation. Dab flux with the thin black stick all over the twisted copper join in the middle.
placements: flux on thin black applicator stick tip → dabbed all over twisted copper join at bottom-center of white wire loop until wet-looking; in the video: bottom-center of loop on blue mat
watch_for: if the join still looks dry and dull you missed spots, dab flux all around the twist
if flux drips onto the mat you used too much, use just enough to wet the copper
3.check_yourself: The twisted copper join in the middle of the white wire loop looks wet with flux.
3.safety: Keep flux off skin and out of eyes, wash hands after.

4.say: Touch the hot soldering-iron tip to the fluxed copper join in the middle. Feed the thin silver solder wire to the join until it melts and spreads along the whole twist.
placements: tinned metal soldering-iron tip set to 350C → touched to fluxed copper join at bottom-center of white loop; in the video: iron from top-center touching bottom-center join
thin silver solder wire 0.5mm → fed from right side to same bottom-center join until silver melts and spreads through wire and round back; in the video: right hand feeds wire to iron tip at join
watch_for: if solder balls up dull and does not spread the join is too cold or lacks flux, reheat with flux
if white insulation melts back you held heat too long, heat only the copper join briefly
4.check_yourself: The center join is fully covered with shiny silver solder joining the white wires with no copper showing.
4.safety: Do not touch the iron tip or fresh solder, hold only the white insulation.

5.say: Push the short black heat-shrink tube onto a free white-wire end. Slide it along the white wire to center it over the silver soldered join.
placements: short black heat-shrink tube about 3.2mm diameter → threaded onto free top end of white wire then slid along white wire to bottom-center to center over silver soldered join; in the video: from top free end slid to bottom-center
watch_for: if silver solder shows at either edge the black tube is off-center, slide it to leave white insulation at both ends
if black tube will not slide over the join it is too small, use larger 3.2mm tube
5.check_yourself: A loose black tube covers the soldered join with white insulation visible on both sides.

6.say: Hold the white wire by the white insulation away from the black tube. Sweep the hot-air gun nozzle gently along the black tube until it shrinks tight.
placements: metal hot-air gun nozzle set to 175C → held just above black tube at bottom-center of white loop and moved gently along sleeving; in the video: large metal nozzle from top-left aimed at bottom-center tube
black heat-shrink tube → shrunk tight around white wire join at bottom-center with white insulation tight at both ends; in the video: bottom-center of blue mat
watch_for: if the black tube still slides the heat was too brief, heat gently again until tight
if white insulation warps or tube browns you overheated one spot, keep the nozzle moving
6.check_yourself: The black sleeve is shrunken tight around the white wire with no solder showing and no sliding.
6.safety: Keep the hot-air nozzle off skin and let the black sleeve cool before touching it.
